issues.summary: TransactionApi.mapError checks nonFieldErrors before the 451 banned-Safe rewrite, so a 451 carrying nonFieldErrors forwards the upstream text
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: src/modules/transactions/datasources/transaction-api.service.ts:1193-1204 returns early from the nonFieldErrors branch, and mapBannedSafeError runs only after it. The PR description says the 451 check runs first and that a test pins the order, but the code at HEAD does neither. The Transaction Service does not currently send this payload shape, so the impact is an unlikely edge case.

issues.summary: The mapBannedSafeError call sites in SafeBalancesApi (getBalance, getCollectibles) and ExportApi have no 451 test
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: The diff contains no safe-balances-api spec, no collectibles integration case and no 451 assertion in export-api.service.spec.ts (it only excludes 451 at :143). Only getBalances (balances.controller.integration.spec.ts:838) and TransactionApi.getSafe are tested, so removing the wrapper at safe-balances-api.service.ts:181/:221 or export-api.service.ts:64 would go unnoticed. The PR description lists these tests, but they are not in this commit.

issues.summary: The loop that draws a random error status other than 451 is copy-pasted across three spec files instead of living in a shared helper
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: The same do/while loop appears in banned-safe.helper.spec.ts:36, export-api.service.spec.ts:143 and as a local function at transaction-api.service.spec.ts:75. The shared src/__tests__/faker.ts helper the PR description mentions is not changed in this diff.

issues.summary: The literal string 'Safe is unavailable for legal reasons' is hard-coded as the upstream detail in five places, where faker would do
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: The literal appears at banned-safe.helper.spec.ts:22 and :69, transaction-api.service.spec.ts:430, balances.controller.integration.spec.ts:857 and safes.controller.integration.spec.ts:2426. The mapper discards the value and nothing asserts on it, which goes against AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (builders + faker, no literal fixtures).

issues.summary: The canonical example in api-dtos-and-validation.md no longer matches the SafeBalancesApi catch sites
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: docs/agents/api-dtos-and-validation.md:121 quotes `throw this.httpErrorFactory.from(error)` for getBalances/getCollectibles. Those lines now read `from(mapBannedSafeError(error))` (safe-balances-api.service.ts:109, :181), so the doc is out of date.

issues.summary: The claim that asserting via mock.calls.length breaks a repo-wide convention
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: No guide under docs/agents requires toHaveBeenCalledTimes (a grep finds nothing), and balances.controller.integration.spec.ts already uses `mock.calls.length` 9 times, so the new test follows local style.

issues.summary: The name mapBannedSafeError is tied to the upstream's cause rather than to the 451 status
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: The PR deliberately scopes the helper to Transaction Service datasources, where 451 always means a banned Safe (banned-safe.helper.ts doc comment, ARCHITECTURE.md addition). Renaming has no concrete benefit today.

issues.summary: There is no dedicated response mapper for SafeBalancesApi errors
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: This is speculative future-proofing. mapBannedSafeError already is the shared mapping seam at safe-balances-api.service.ts:109, and nothing currently needs more handling.

issues.summary: Tests build the error with `{ status } as Response` instead of a real Response
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: `as Response` casts are the existing pattern for building NetworkResponseError across the repo's specs (for example the pre-existing TransactionApi cases). The new test at safes.controller.integration.spec.ts:2424 follows that pattern at no concrete cost.

issues.summary: The local helper sits between the describe-scoped const and let declarations
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: transaction-api.service.spec.ts:70-83 places the function inside describe before the `let` block. This is purely a layout preference with no functional effect.
